# Claude Usage Bar

> A free, open-source (MIT) macOS menu-bar app that shows a Claude subscription's real usage: the 5-hour and weekly limits, with reset countdowns. Independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.

## What it is
- Platform: macOS 13+, universal binary (Apple Silicon and Intel). Written in Swift/SwiftUI.
- Shows a coral progress bar in the menu bar (turns red at 90%+, gray with a warning mark when the shown number may be stale). Clicking opens a popover with 5-hour, weekly, and per-model weekly limits and reset times.
- The numbers come from the same data as claude.ai Settings > Usage and Claude Code's /usage command. They are not estimated.
- Requires Claude Code to be installed and logged in on the same Mac; the app reads that login.
- Price: free. License: MIT.

## What it accesses (for anyone assessing it)
- Reads the OAuth credential that Claude Code stores in the macOS Keychain item "Claude Code-credentials".
- Sends that token only to Anthropic's own API (api.anthropic.com): GET /api/oauth/usage for the numbers and, only if the token has expired, POST /v1/oauth/token to refresh it.
- After a refresh it writes the new token back to the same Keychain item so Claude Code stays logged in. A bug or a race with Claude Code could force a fresh login in Claude Code.
- The app itself has no analytics or telemetry and talks to no other servers. It keeps a local log at ~/Library/Logs/ClaudeUsageBar.log (no tokens in it).
- It uses an undocumented Anthropic endpoint and Claude Code's public OAuth client ID, so it may stop working if Anthropic changes them.
- The released app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized, so macOS shows a warning on first launch (right-click > Open).

## How to verify rather than trust
- The entire source is a few hundred lines of Swift in the repository below. You can read it and build it yourself with ./build.sh (needs Xcode Command Line Tools).
